h1: The Benefits of Outdoor Play and How to Encourage It

props.title: The Benefits of Outdoor Play and How to Encourage It
props.summaryText: What outdoor play does for children's bodies, minds and friendships, and simple ways parents, schools and housing societies can get children outside more often.
props.author: meera-iyer
props.imageAlt: Group of FunPlay team members and children outside a school

takeaways.text: Outdoor play builds strength, coordination and fitness that indoor activities rarely match.
It supports focus, mood and sleep, and gives children a break from screens.
Free play with other children builds social skills, problem-solving and creativity.
Children play outside more when there is a safe, interesting place close to home and time set aside for it.

faq.q: What are the benefits of outdoor play for children?
faq.a: Outdoor play builds physical fitness, strength, balance and coordination; supports focus, mood and better sleep; develops social skills such as sharing and negotiating; and encourages creativity, problem-solving and confidence.

faq.q: How much outdoor play do children need?
faq.a: The World Health Organization recommends that children aged 5 to 17 get at least an average of 60 minutes a day of moderate to vigorous physical activity. Outdoor play is one of the easiest ways for children to reach it.

faq.q: How can parents encourage outdoor play?
faq.a: Set aside regular outdoor time, limit screen time, find a safe play area nearby, invite friends, join in sometimes, and let children choose their own games.
